content:
#1 At “Definition as a 2-functor”, the article says

For a proarrow H ⁣:B→DH\colon B\to DH:B→D and ordinary arrows f ⁣:A→Bf\colon A\to Bf:A→B and g ⁣:C→Dg\colon C\to Dg:C→D, we write H(g,f)H(g,f)H(g,f) for the composite D(g,1)∘H∘B(1,f)D(g,1) \circ H \circ B(1,f)D(g,1)∘H∘B(1,f); it is a proarrow from AAA to CCC. We also write UAU_AUA​, A(1,1)A(1,1)A(1,1), or simply AAA for the identity proarrow A↛AA\nrightarrow AA↛A.

In seems that the nLab has settled on the convention that a profunctor H ⁣:B↛DH\colon B\nrightarrow DH:B↛D is a functor H ⁣:Dop×B→SetH\colon D^{\mathrm{op}} \times B \to {\mathrm{Set}}H:Dop×B→Set. Therefore, in the expressions H(g,f)H(g, f)H(g,f) and B(1,f)B(1, f)B(1,f) the morphism fff is in the covariant slot, which means that either fff should be a morphism out of BBB or HHH should be a profunctor into AAA.

What am I missing?
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #2 It seems right to me. The covariant slot of HHH is the category that it is “from” as a profunctor, and we are substituting a value of fff into that slot; so it’s correct that HHH is a profunctor from BBB to something else, and that the values of fff belong to BBB, i.e. that fff is a morphism into BBB.
subject: Proarrow equipment

content:
#3 In that case, DDD and ggg are the problem. Thinking of HHH as a set of heteromorphisms from BBB to DDD, we can precompose with fff to get a set of heteromorphisms from AAA to DDD, but to postcompose, we need g ⁣:D→Cg\colon D \to Cg:D→C, not g ⁣:C→Dg\colon C \to Dg:C→D. That is,

H(f ⁣:A→B,g ⁣:D→C)(h ⁣:B→D)=g∘h∘f ⁣:A→C.H(f\colon A\to B, g\colon D \to C)(h\colon B \to D) = g \circ h \circ f\colon A \to C.H(f:A→B,g:D→C)(h:B→D)=g∘h∘f:A→C.
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #4 fff is not a morphism in BBB, it’s a functor with codomain BBB, and similarly ggg is not a morphism in DDD, it’s a functor with codomain DDD. We’re not describing the action of the functor HHH on its elements/heteromorphisms; we’re describing its restriction along a pair of functors.
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #5 It’s like the multiplication of three matrices (the outer two being special in deriving from functions), if that helps. Or the composition of relations.
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #6 Mike: Then shouldn’t it be D(1,g)∘H∘B(1,f)D(1, g) \circ H \circ B(1,f)D(1,g)∘H∘B(1,f), that is, fff followed by HHH followed by the taking the preimage under ggg? The expression D(g,1)D(g, 1)D(g,1) doesn’t make sense; since BBB is the codomain of fff, having ggg in the other slot means we’d want the domain of ggg. If we want the codomain of ggg, it needs to be in the same slot that fff is.
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #7 The DDD in D(g,1)D(g,1)D(g,1) represents the hom-functor of DDD, which is a profunctor from DDD to DDD. Thus, ggg being a functor with codomain DDD, it can be plugged into either slot of this profunctor.
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #8 Although in the context of the quote in question, D(1,g)D(1,g)D(1,g) and D(g,1)D(g,1)D(g,1) are just notations for the two proarrows associated to the arrow ggg. The reason for using that notation is as I said: in the case of categories and profunctors, they are (x,y)↦HomD(x,g(y))(x,y) \mapsto {\mathrm{Hom}}_D(x,g(y))(x,y)↦HomD​(x,g(y)) and (y,x)↦HomD(g(y),x)(y,x) \mapsto {\mathrm{Hom}}_D(g(y),x)(y,x)↦HomD​(g(y),x).
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #9 OK, so in that notation, both slots are covariant. I’ll add a note to that effect. Thanks!
subject: Proarrow equipment

content: #10 I think I have some idea of what you mean, but I don’t think “both slots are covariant” is really the correct way to say it. HHH is still a functor from Dop×BD^{\mathrm{op}}\times BDop×B to Set\mathrm{Set}Set, so in that sense the first slot is contravariant. And if the question is what kind of a functor H(g,f)H(g,f)H(g,f) is as a functor of ggg and fff, then it’s a functor from K(A,B)op×K(C,D)K(A,B)^{\mathrm{op}}\times K(C,D)K(A,B)op×K(C,D) to M(A,C)M(A,C)M(A,C), so in that sense also the first slot is contravariant.
